To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the coherent electronic charge transfer between the donor and acceptor is observed in a supramolecular system on the femtosecond time scale, 2) the vibrational modes that drive the coupling of the electronic states are not optically accessed and 3) this is the first example of coherent electronic charge beating observed in a superramolecular system at ambient conditions.
we were able to characterize the early dynamics of electronic coherence in a large molecular system, a rhodamine dimer, by means of ultrafast two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy.
the electronic coherence built upon the optical excitation of a supramolecular rhodomine heterodimer-DNAscaffold is preserved up to 150 fs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the role of quantum coherence and the mechanisms of energy transfer in multichromophore systems.
understanding the basic mechanisms of light-harving in biological and artificial supramolecular complexes.
understanding and controlling the dynamics of electronic and vibrational coherences in artificial multichromopohoric antenna systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
electronic coherences in the rhodamine hetero-dimer are not the result of a vibrational coupling, but rather a direct consequence of the coherent electronic coupling of the two dyes in the dimer.

, although electronic coherences are not the only mechanism for energy migration, they are a key ingredient in the energy transfer dynamics of supramolecular antenna systems, and that their role can be experimentally identified.
electronic and nuclear quantum coherences can be observed in the early times of the electronic excitation of supramolecular complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown the possibility to observe electronic coherence in a supramolecular system and that the vibrational mode driving the electronic coherence is not the mode responsible for the electronic coupling.

the electronic coherences in the rhodamine heterochromophoric system can be observed for a time scale of 150 fs, which corresponds to the period of the vibrational modes that are involved in the coupling between electronic states.
we have been able to observe a coherent electronic and nuclear dynamics within a supramolecular complex at room temperature in solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the coherent electronic and nuclear dynamics of the supramolecular complex can be described in a simple way, without invoking the presence of a quantum superposition state of the entire dyes, as the electronic and nuclear dynamics can be understood in a sequential manner.

the coherent electronic and vibrational dynamics are decoupled in the supramolecular complex, which allows the electronic coherence to be maintained for 150 fs, much longer than the electronic coherence lifetime in the free rhodamine hetero-dimer.
the electronic coherence built on a supramolecular system can be preserved for more than 100 fs at room temperature, which is longer than the electronic coherence in a molecular system.
